typical_symptoms: Clustered aggregations of small bugs inside opening cotton bolls
Brownish or dirty yellowish staining of white cotton lint
Damage to cotton seeds resulting in shriveling and weight reduction
Lint contamination from crushed bug bodies and excrement during harvest
visual_characteristics: Small, dark brown to black elongated insects with clear translucent wings resting on white cotton fibers
Nymphs appearing as small reddish-orange to dark brown wingless insects in clusters
Localized brownish smears or stains visible on cotton lint locules
lesion_characteristics: Pinpoint puncture marks on seed coats
Irregular yellowish-brown staining spots on lint without chlorotic halos
Dried, shriveled necrotic seeds inside affected bolls
color_characteristics: Adult insects feature dark brown/black bodies with whitish-hyaline transparent wings
Nymphs progress from light reddish-orange to dark brown
Lint transitions from bright white to dull brown or yellowish-brown stained
texture_characteristics: Dry fibrous lint interwoven with insect bodies and greasy staining residue
spatial_patterns: Dense clusters inside the crevices of opened boll carpels and lint locules
Irregular, patchy staining spread across fiber surfaces
distinguishing_features: Direct presence of small, dark brown bugs with transparent wings embedded within open white cotton bolls
Characteristic dirty lint staining due to crushed bug fluids rather than leaf-borne fungal lesions
